meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Извините, а как часто мы должны?
examples.trans: Excuse me, and how often should we try?

examples.text: Что вы говорите? А это вам зачем?
examples.trans: What are you saying? And why do you need that?

examples.text: А это Канат, он у нас киргиз.
examples.trans: And this is Kanat, he is our Kyrgyz cook.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'salt', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Regular cooks are the salt of the kitchen earth.
Did you not forget the salt?
Onion, salt, pepper — and that's all.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('not') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Давно ты обычным поваром не трудился.
examples.trans: You haven't worked as an ordinary cook in a long time.
I simply did not get enough sleep.
I have not lost my edge at all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (root 'быть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to forget', forming an aspectual pair with 'забывать'.

examples.trans: Did you forget what the doctor said?
Did you not forget the salt?
I did not forget anything at all.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('yes') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I simply did not get enough sleep.

examples.text: За этими золотыми руками иногда нужен глаз да глаз.
examples.trans: Though you have to keep a very close eye on those golden hands.
Yes, Chef!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('nothing') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: I have not lost my edge at all.

examples.text: Ничего страшного. Судя по анализам, вы здоровы.
examples.trans: Nothing terrible. Judging by the tests, you are healthy.

examples.text: Трудно работать в команде, когда ни о ком ничего не знаешь.
examples.trans: It is hard to work in a team when you know nothing about anyone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('I') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: I simply did not get enough sleep.
I have not lost my edge at all.

examples.text: Я даже не знаю значения этого слова.
examples.trans: I do not even know the meaning of that word.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: Well, what does it say?

examples.text: Что вы говорите? А это вам зачем?
examples.trans: What are you saying? And why do you need that?

examples.text: Жена вчера запилила, что поздно пришёл.
examples.trans: His wife nagged him yesterday for coming home late.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Давно ты обычным поваром не трудился.
examples.trans: You haven't worked as an ordinary cook in a long time.
You have lost your edge, old timer.
You are talking to a tomato.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.trans: They have the hardest job of all.

examples.text: Всю морковку почистили, ещё дудку сделали. Молодец.
examples.trans: You peeled all the carrots and even made a flute. Well done.

examples.text: Да потому что это происходит всё время.
examples.trans: Because this happens all the time.

контролировать.gloss: to control, to keep an eye on

meanings.en: to control, to keep an eye on
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to control', forming an aspectual pair with 'проконтролировать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: They control the situation.
Why are you controlling everything in here?
I'm supposed to keep an eye on you!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.

examples.text: Я решила, ты тут с Денисом надолго зависнешь.
examples.trans: I figured you would be stuck here with Denis for a long time.
We will manage fine here.
Why are you controlling everything in here?

ходить.gloss: to walk, to go (on foot, regularly)

meanings.en: to walk, to go (on foot, regularly)
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to walk'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: You have been following me around all day.
The boy walks on crutches.
I walk to work.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'day', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: В ближайшие два дня советую вам хорошенько потрудиться.
examples.trans: Over the next two days I advise you to work really hard.

examples.text: Имеется в виду за два дня.
examples.trans: I mean over the course of two days.

examples.text: Любимая, у нас впереди целых два дня.
examples.trans: Darling, we have two whole days ahead of us.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Имеется в виду за два дня.
examples.trans: I mean over the course of two days.

examples.text: За этими золотыми руками иногда нужен глаз да глаз.
examples.trans: Though you have to keep a very close eye on those golden hands.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'a lot'.

examples.text: Да я вижу, у вас много времени.
examples.trans: Yes, I can see that you have plenty of free time.

meanings.en: to attend to, take care of, engage in
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (root 'няться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to attend to', forming an aspectual pair with 'заниматься'.

examples.trans: Do you have nothing else to do?
Handle the money, Mayor!
I will take care of this question tomorrow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('nothing') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: Do you have nothing else to do?
Do you have nothing to do?

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'идти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: And if you don't finish in time, out you go.

examples.text: Пойди в салон красоты, что-нибудь сделай.
examples.trans: Go to a beauty salon, do something for yourself.

examples.text: Пойди в салон красоты, что-нибудь сделай.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('something') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Пойди в салон красоты, что-нибудь сделай.

examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (root 'делать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to do', forming an aspectual pair with 'делать'.

examples.text: Никак не может себе сделать гражданство.
examples.trans: He just cannot manage to get his citizenship.

examples.text: Поразительно. Это вы сами сделали? Из морковки?
examples.trans: Astonishing. Did you make this yourself? Out of a carrot?

examples.text: Всю морковку почистили, ещё дудку сделали. Молодец.
examples.trans: You peeled all the carrots and even made a flute. Well done.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (root 'винить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to excuse', forming an aspectual pair with 'извинять'.

examples.trans: Oops, sorry, out of habit.

examples.text: Извините, а как часто мы должны?
examples.trans: Excuse me, and how often should we try?

examples.text: Извините. Я просто хотел извиниться за то, что наорал на тебя.
examples.trans: Sorry. I just wanted to apologize for yelling at you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('something') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: Sorry, I got carried away...

examples.text: Что такое? Вам что-то не нравится?
examples.trans: What is it? Is there something you do not like?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'massage', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна приказала сделать ей массаж ног!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to wish', forming an aspectual pair with 'пожелать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Would you care for a massage as well?

examples.trans: From this moment on, report to vegetable prep.

examples.text: Заготовка на завтра сама себя сделает?
examples.trans: Will tomorrow's prep do itself?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to peel', forming an aspectual pair with 'почистить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Глупо чистить двадцать мешков картошки. Зачем?
examples.trans: It is foolish to peel twenty sacks of potatoes. What for?
Go peel potatoes.
Peeling potatoes by the sack?

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'potatoes', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Вам не составит большого труда почистить мешок картошки.
examples.trans: It will not be much trouble for you to peel a sack of potatoes.

examples.text: Герман Михайлович, а для чего нам нужно столько картошки?
examples.trans: German Mikhailovich, why do we need so many potatoes?

examples.text: Герман попросил до вечера почистить два мешка картошки.
examples.trans: German asked me to peel two sacks of potatoes before evening.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.

examples.trans: I understand. Well, alright.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'work', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
